decisions.title: Adopt the proposal as a whole
decisions.summary: The proposal to add a new special form `TypeIs` for user-defined type narrowing functions was accepted.
decisions.rationale: The community largely favored `TypeIs` over other alternatives, with `IsInstance` as a close second. The name was chosen to align with existing runtime functionality and to avoid confusion with other Python concepts.

decisions.title: Name of the new special form
decisions.summary: The new special form `TypeIs` behaves similarly to `TypeGuard`, but without the backward-incompatible changes proposed in PEP 724.
decisions.rationale: The name `TypeIs` was chosen due to its clear and concise nature, and it received consensus from the participants. The name `TypeIs` is short and reads well, making it a preferred choice over alternatives like `TypeCheck`, `Narrowed`, `IsInstance`, and `ForceTypeIs`.

decisions.title: Compatibility with existing TypeGuard
decisions.summary: The new TypeNarrower construct is designed to be compatible with existing TypeGuard, with both constructs having the same specification for all aspects not related to type narrowing behavior.
decisions.rationale: The PEP aims to avoid backwards compatibility issues by creating a new special form and leaving TypeGuard unchanged. The design choice is to make TypeNarrower and TypeGuard behave as similarly as possible, with the PEP recommending that TypeGuard be reserved for rare cases where its behavior is specifically desired.

evidence.quote: I don’t find the objections raised against `TypeIs` strongly persuasive. In my experience, it is very common when discussing Python types to say something like “the type of `x` is `int`,” where the obvious meaning is the same as `x: int`, that is “x is an instance of `int` or a subtype.” I’ve never seen this wording lead someone to believe that the type of `x` must be exactly int; a concept that isn’t even representable in Python type annotations.

decisions.title: Whether to add a ForceTypeIs variant
decisions.summary: The discussion did not reach a consensus on adding a `ForceTypeIs` variant.
decisions.rationale: Some participants suggested adding a `ForceTypeIs` variant to avoid confusion, but others argued that it would be as easy to accidentally use one over the other as it would be to write an incorrect type narrower in the first place.

evidence.quote: Could type checker check if `ForceTypeIs` is redundant over `TypeIs`? In this case a warning could be emitted. It’s probably not that straightforward to implement, though.
evidence.author: PawelSwiecki

evidence.quote: Could type checkers detect unsound `TypeIs` (and `TypeGuard`) functions? Maybe in a few cases, but I don’t expect this to be possible in general. If type checkers add the ability to detect some unsound narrowing functions, we could mention that in the user-facing documentation later. I certainly don’t want to prohibit type checkers from trying.
evidence.author: Jelle

evidence.quote: With `TypeIs` vs `ForceTypeIs` it becomes just as easy to accidentally use one over the other as it would be to write an incorrect type narrower in the first place, so I don’t think it’s a big enough win personally.
